findings.title: _skimSurplusBatch over-skim via duplicate clients[] under-backs principal
findings.description: A duplicated address in the caller-supplied clients[] is counted once per occurrence (no dedup at :476), ceilinged only by total held shares (:481). The aggregate swap sells into the pool backing OTHER clients' principal while clientBalances is intentionally untouched, silently under-backing principal. INV-1 (totalDeposited == sum(clientBalances)) still holds, so the loss is invisible in principal accounting and shows up only in share backing. Trigger is gated by onlyAuthorizedWithdrawer (trusted role), realistic via an accidental duplicate; no external attacker and no direct theft, so capped at Medium below the C4 High bar.

findings.title: NAV-anchored minOut is execution-price-blind, enabling sandwich value leak
findings.description: minOut = idealUnderlying * (MAX_BPS - bps) / MAX_BPS is derived from the vault's convertToAssets (sUSDe NAV), independent of the Curve pool the trade actually clears on (the adapter forwards the floor verbatim). A NAV-anchored floor cannot detect a skewed pool; a sandwich can extract up to bps * tradeSize per swap, and the absence of a swap deadline widens the window. sUSDe NAV is not atomically flash-loan manipulable (that framing dismissed). Conditional value leak under public-mempool plus profitable-pool-skew assumptions with an external MEV requirement — Medium.

M-03 (requested-not-received decrement socialising slippage) was determined by poc-generator and poc-validator to have no standalone loss primitive — on a correctly-collateralized pool it produces zero loss — and only amplifies this NAV-anchored slippage leak by concentrating the share-backing deficit onto the last withdrawer. Both PoCs (poc-M02-nav-sandwich.t.sol, poc-M03-socialized-slippage.t.sol) support this finding. Core mechanism: NAV-anchored minOut is execution-price-blind; value accrues to external MEV, with the amplification path socialising the residual deficit across clients.

findings.title: Requested-not-received decrement socialises slippage, causing last-withdrawer shortfall
findings.description: _withdrawInternal sells convertToShares(amount) at fair NAV but executes worse, then debits clientBalances/totalDeposited by the full REQUESTED amount (:333-336). Shares worth more than the principal removed leave the pool, so backing erodes faster than the ledger (INV-1 still holds). Over adverse cycles a late withdrawer hits the sharesToSell > availableShares cap (:316-318) and silently recovers less than the principal debited. Cross-client principal loss, opposite beneficiary to M-02 (here loss is socialised across clients, not captured by external MEV), bounded by cumulative slippage.

findings.title: slippageToleranceBps default-0 plus setter missing sane cap (missing validation)
findings.description: (a) No initializer for slippageToleranceBps (:40) means it defaults to 0, so minOut == ideal and swaps revert until an owner configures it (availability-until-configured, fixed by one owner call). (b) setSlippageTolerance (:190-195) checks only _bps <= MAX_BPS with no sane upper cap (Halmos: bps == MAX_BPS => minOut == 0). Pure missing-validation finding; the 'owner sets 100%' narrative is an excluded reckless-admin framing and NOT the stated impact, so QA/Low.
findings.notes: Impact must remain framed as missing validation, per classifier note.

findings.title: _skimSurplusBatch whole-batch revert on single zero-address entry plus unbounded clients[]
findings.description: require(client != address(0)) inside the loop (:470) reverts the entire batch, inconsistent with the graceful continue used for principal==0 / surplus==0 entries. Combined with an unbounded caller-supplied array. Self-inflicted by a trusted caller, no third-party harm and no asset loss — QA/Low.
findings.notes: Behavioural inconsistency / robustness, not an asset-loss path.
